items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I remember that album that he did for Joe Turner has those kind of arrangements.

ctx.x: And Joe’s hit, he had that hit “Every Day I Have the Blues.” It was about that time, wasn’t it?

Well when he came, the first time he came through with the band, he had I think maybe four really strong arrangements. He had “Every Day,” he had “In the Evening When the Sun Goes Down,” he had “The Comeback,” and I can’t remember what else. I know Frank Foster had done something for him and Ernie Wilkins had done something for him. And they were just ideal arrangements. Ernie had that understanding of the old riff patterns that grew up in the old Basie band, and he was able to write new stuff that called up that…
It’s a real skill to be able to write something that comes from really, if it was just played from the top of your head, to try to put that on paper. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
